# Schema: FairScreen

No database. Parsed resumes live in memory; the fixture is generated files.

## Fixture layout (generated by `sample_data/generate.py`, not committed)

```
sample_data/out/
├── resumes/*.txt          # 24 synthetic resumes
└── metadata.csv           # filename, name, group (gender_by_name), tier, experience_years
```

The metadata is ground truth for the audit demonstration: it is generated,
known, and clearly labeled synthetic. Real uploads have no such labels; the
audit section only activates with metadata present.

## In-memory records

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| filename | str | display name |
| text | str | extracted text (redacted when the toggle is on) |
| redactions | list[str] | what was removed (categories, not values) |
| proxies | list[str] | detected proxy categories with the matched fragment |
| score / text_similarity / skill_coverage | float | match components |
| gaps | list[str] | JD skills missing from this resume |
| group | str \| None | from metadata.csv only |

## CSV export columns

`rank, filename, group, score, text_similarity, skill_coverage, gaps, proxies`

## Security policies

- No secrets in this project; env vars are a flag and a cutoff.
- Redaction runs before ranking; when enabled, raw text never renders.
- Fixture and uploads are gitignored; nothing persists from the app session.
